info.title: vm-intent API
info.description:
Request virtual machines on vSphere, AWS, Azure or Google Cloud, in plain English or as an exact spec.

**How it works.** Every request becomes one canonical, cloud-neutral spec with a SHA-256 hash. The same spec can't be built twice at once: the hash is the build's identity. A Temporal workflow builds each VM and rolls it back (deletes it) if anything fails.

**Typical flows**
- *One VM, with a human in the loop:* `POST /api/v2/requests`, poll `GET /api/v2/requests/{id}`, then `/clarify` if it asks a question and `/confirm` to build.
- *Many VMs from a service:* `POST /api/v2/batches` with specs or text, then poll `GET /api/v2/batches/{id}`. No confirmation step per VM.
- *Check first:* `POST /api/v2/interpret` shows what a text would become, without building anything.

**Optional fields.** Fields with no value are left out of responses rather than sent as null.

**Errors.** Every 4xx and 5xx response has the body `{"error": "..."}`.

**Sign-in.** Off on this server: restrict access at the network level. See the "Required role" on each operation for what applies when sign-in is on.

post.summary: Start a run of a definition
post.description:
Checks the inputs, fills in defaults and starts the run. The run's ID comes from the definition version and the inputs, so sending the same thing again finds the run already going (200, existing=true) instead of starting a second one.

**Required role:** REQUESTER (when sign-in is on; it is currently off)

200.description: A run with the same definition version and inputs is already going

post.description:
Undoes everything the run did, newest step first (including the failed step's partial work). For a run stopped after a failure or waiting for an approval. The run's requester or an operator.

**Required role:** REQUESTER (when sign-in is on; it is currently off)

409.description: Not in a state that can be torn down

post.description:
Runs the failed step again (it picks up whatever its last try did), then carries on. The run's requester or an operator. 409 if the run isn't stopped after a failure.

**Required role:** REQUESTER (when sign-in is on; it is currently off)

post.summary: Approve or reject a waiting step
post.description:
Anyone but the run's requester, and only someone on the step's approvers list if it has one.

**Required role:** REQUESTER (when sign-in is on; it is currently off)

get.description:
Newest first, filtered by any of: requester, state, provider, env. Uses Temporal search attributes; if the Temporal server doesn't have them, filters are refused (400) and only the unfiltered list works. The state is the last one the request reported.

**Required role:** READER (when sign-in is on; it is currently off)

post.description:
Starts a request workflow for one VM. Poll GET /api/v2/requests/{id}: when state is AWAITING_CLARIFICATION, answer the question; when AWAITING_CONFIRMATION, confirm or cancel. Both waits time out after 24 hours.

**Required role:** REQUESTER (when sign-in is on; it is currently off)

Use when state is AWAITING_CONFIRMATION, after the requester has checked the spec. Send the specHash you were shown to make sure it's the spec being built. Answers with the request's new status (PROVISIONING, or DUPLICATE if the VM already exists).

**Required role:** REQUESTER (when sign-in is on; it is currently off)

403.description: Not your request (sign-in on, not an admin)

post.description:

get.description:
Results of the nightly check (and any run by hand), newest first: VMs that disappeared from their cloud (now MISSING) and VMs in a cloud that nobody recorded (orphans; never deleted automatically). Clouds behind the one-way link are skipped.

**Required role:** READER (when sign-in is on; it is currently off)

post.summary: Preview how a request is understood
post.description:
Turns plain English into the canonical spec and its hash, or returns the question it would ask. Starts nothing and builds nothing. Many wordings of the same VM give the same specHash.

**Required role:** REQUESTER (when sign-in is on; it is currently off)

post.summary: Publish a definition sent as JSON
post.description:
Operators only. A published version never changes: publish a higher version to change it. Publishing the same version with the same content again does nothing (UNCHANGED), so a pipeline can publish every file on every merge.

**Required role:** OPERATOR (when sign-in is on; it is currently off)

No new runs of it; runs already going carry on. retired=false brings it back.

**Required role:** OPERATOR (when sign-in is on; it is currently off)

post.summary: Check a definition sent as JSON
post.description:
Send the YAML (Content-Type: application/yaml or text/plain), or JSON {"yaml": "..."}. Every problem is listed at once: names, actions and their settings, every CEL expression, and that steps only read earlier steps. Used by the Git pipeline before a merge.

**Required role:** REQUESTER (when sign-in is on; it is currently off)

Copies closed histories to the archive and removes what is past its retention. It also runs every hour on the vm-archive-sweep schedule.

**Required role:** ADMIN (when sign-in is on; it is currently off)

post.summary: Replay a recorded workflow for audit
post.description:
Runs today's code against the recorded history without doing anything again: no cloud calls, no files, no database writes. matches=true shows the recorded run is exactly what this code does. Uses the archive (SHA-256 checked) or, if it isn't archived yet, Temporal.

**Required role:** AUDITOR (when sign-in is on; it is currently off)

404.description: No such workflow in the archive or Temporal

post.description:
Every item is checked before anything starts. Items that need a clarifying answer, or break policy, are returned in `rejected`; the rest are built with no confirmation step. An item identical to another (same spec hash) is built once. Poll GET /api/v2/batches/{id}.

**Required role:** BATCH (when sign-in is on; it is currently off)

400.description: Empty, too large, or no item could be built

post.summary: Create a VM from the legacy JSON format
post.description:
The old universal JSON definition. Skips interpretation and confirmation and goes straight to the build. Kept for existing callers; new callers should use /api/v2.

**Required role:** BATCH (when sign-in is on; it is currently off)

get.description:
Count VMs by state

**Required role:** READER (when sign-in is on; it is currently off)

Live from the run's workflow: every step, what it produced, and what the run is waiting for.

**Required role:** READER (when sign-in is on; it is currently off)

state is one of STARTING, INTERPRETING, AWAITING_CLARIFICATION, AWAITING_CONFIRMATION, PROVISIONING, COMPLETED, PARTIAL, FAILED, CANCELLED, DUPLICATE, or BUSY (workers didn't answer within 5 seconds; try again). The final states are COMPLETED, PARTIAL, FAILED, CANCELLED and DUPLICATE. A request for several VMs ends COMPLETED when none failed (VMs that already existed count as running) and PARTIAL when some were built and some failed.

**Required role:** READER (when sign-in is on; it is currently off)

kind = Provisioning or Blueprint. version 0 (the default) = the newest.

**Required role:** READER (when sign-in is on; it is currently off)

Every authorization decision, newest first: who asked to do what, ALLOW or DENY, and the rule that decided. Each is kept for its classification's retention.

**Required role:** AUDITOR (when sign-in is on; it is currently off)

memoryGiB.description: Current memory in GiB (after any resize).

owner.description: Who owns the VM: the person who asked for it.

history.description: Timestamped lifecycle events, newest last (the last 50).

items.description: Timestamped lifecycle events, newest last (the last 50).

ResizeBody.description: A new size for a VM.

PowerBody.description: Power a VM on or off.

version.description: A version; empty = the newest that isn't retired.

classification.description: Data classification code; empty = the definition's. Can raise the definition's retention, not lower it.

requestedBy.description: Who is asking, when sign-in is off.

RunBody.description: Start a run of a definition.

Approval.description: An approval step that is waiting.

retentionYears.description: Years to keep histories and decision logs (1-5).

Classification.description: A data classification: a code with its text. The code decides how long the run, its history and its access decisions are kept.

existing.description: true = a run with these inputs already existed

RunStarted.description: A run that has started, or the one already running with the same inputs.

failedStep.description: The step that failed, while waiting for a decision.

recoveryDeadline.description: When the run tears itself down if nobody decides (ISO-8601).

attempts.description: Tries so far, counting every resume.

additionalProperties.description: What the step produced; later steps read it as steps.<id>.

output.description: What the step produced; later steps read it as steps.<id>.

note.example: the site files are in the store now

text.description: What you want, in your own words.
text.example: Ubuntu box, 4 cores, 16 gigs, us-east on AWS

userId.description: Who is asking. Recorded in the audit trail.

TextBody.description: A VM request in plain English.

requestId.description: ID to use with the other /requests endpoints.

specHash.description: The specHash you were shown. If given and it doesn't match, the confirmation is refused (409), so nobody confirms a spec they didn't see.

ConfirmBody.description: Confirm the spec a request is waiting on.

specHash.description: The VM's identity: the SHA-256 of the canonical spec. For a signed-in user the hash also covers the user ID, so each user gets their own VM.

question.description: Set when something must be answered before a spec can be built.
question.example: Which platform should this run on: vSphere (on-prem), AWS, Azure or Google Cloud?

count.description: How many identical VMs were asked for. Left out when it's one.

cloudName.description: The VM's name in its cloud: the same as spec.name, except that a signed-in user's named VM gets '-' plus the first 8 characters of specHash after it (web-01-3af19a4e). Left out when a question is asked.

Interpretation.description: What a request was understood to mean. Either spec/specHash are set, or question is.

message.description: Human-readable status, or the question being asked.

vms.description: Every VM of a request for more than one (count > 1), in order.

RequestStatus.description: Where a request is, and what it understood.

VmResult.description: The built VM, in the provider's own terms.

name.description: VM name. Generated from the hash if left empty.

region.description: Cloud regions: us-east, us-west, us-central, eu-west. vSphere datacenters: dc1, dc2.

VmSpec.description: The canonical, cloud-neutral VM spec. Its SHA-256 (specHash) is the VM's identity.

AnswerBody.description: An answer to the question a request is waiting on.

problems.description: Why it was refused: every problem found, each as 'where: what'.

items.description: Why it was refused: every problem found, each as 'where: what'.

YamlBody.description: A definition as YAML, for clients that can only send JSON.

RetireBody.description: Stop (or allow again) new runs of one version.

appliesWhen.description: CEL condition: the blueprint also applies to every catalog VM for which this is true. Empty = only to definitions that name it.

check.description: CEL condition that must be true.

message.example: Production VMs need at least 2 vCPU.

version.description: Goes up by one each time it's published.

owner.description: Who looks after this definition (team or person).

classification.description: Default data classification code for its runs.

blueprint.description: Blueprint whose rules every VM it builds must pass, or empty.

recoveryWaitHours.description: Hours a failed run waits for Resume or Tear down before it tears itself down (1-720, i.e. up to 30 days; 720 when the definition doesn't say).

sourceSha256.description: SHA-256 of the YAML it was read from.

DefinitionView.description: A published version, as data and as the YAML it was published from.

defaultValue.description: Used when the input isn't given.

allowed.description: If set, the value must be one of these.

items.description: If set, the value must be one of these.

title.description: Shown in the run's step list.

when.description: CEL condition; the step is skipped when it's false.

requestedBy.description: Who is asking. Recorded in the audit trail.
